runtime: CPython 3.13.5. A fresh fixture executes once, single-threaded; all observations precede interpreter teardown.
instructions: Predict the named observation fields from the supplied specification. Identify any component the text leaves unresolved. State ordered events and state changes unambiguously.
fixture_semantics: rec creates a fresh standard LogRecord with the stated name and levelno 12. Whenever Python truth-tests the caller-provided Receiver, its __bool__ appends a check event, raises ArithmeticError while ready is false and returns True while ready is true. Its handle appends one handle event and returns True; it performs no other action. Events accumulate from construction. state copies the current event list and record names, then checks target identity with the receiver and with None; the identity comparisons do not truth-test the receiver. No event list entry is mutated after creation. outcome calls its argument once and reports either 'ok' or the caught exception class name.

questions.question: What is the result of close, what state can be observed immediately afterward, and what does the last flush leave?
questions.stimulus_python:
t = Receiver()
h = MemoryHandler(6, flushLevel=80)
h.emit(rec("north"))
h.emit(rec("south"))
h.setTarget(t)
closed = outcome(h.close)
after = state(h, t)
t.ready = True
h.setTarget(t)
drained = outcome(h.flush)
observations = {"close_outcome": closed, "after_close": after, "after_recovery": [drained, state(h, t)]}
